newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish 96/97 Aegean cotton output seen at record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish 96/97 Aegean cotton output seen at record.

text.p: Cotton output in Turkey's leading Aegean region is expected to reach a 17-year high of 308,292 tonnes in 1996/97 (Oct-July), against 307,733 in 1995/96, the Izmir Trade Bourse (ITB) said on Wednesday.
According to a joint study by ITB, Aegean cotton exporters and producers' unions, the cultivated area rose slightly to 266,424 hectares, up 187 ha on 1995/96.

Initial predictions by Turkey's three trade bourses had put 1996/97 cotton output at 299,157 tonnes for the Aegean, 227,861 tonnes for the southeast region, 225,217 tonnes for southern Cukurova region and 31,500 tonnes for southern Antalya province.
No revisions have so far been made in other regions.
Turkish cotton production was initially forecasted at 783,735 tonnes for 1996/97, down from 837,114 in 1995/96, but will increase in line with the Aegean revision.
"Satisfactory cotton prices were an important factor in raising output," the ITB said in a statement, adding that the removal of a cotton export levy also helped.
The government removed a 20 cent/kg cotton export levy in December 1995 after reducing it from 60 cents in November.
The move allowed excess cotton stocks to be exported and raised domestic prices by some 25 percent to match world levels.
Aegean cotton is said to have the best quality in Turkey, but the southeast, where a huge irrigation and energy project is under way, is rapidly catching up in quality and quantity.

About 125,000 hectares of land has been opened to irrigation in the southeast since early 1995 within the scope of the $32 billion Southeast Anatolian Project (GAP), which will be fully operational after 2000.
Cotton output in the southeast stood at 210,810 tonnes in 1995/96 and is expected to rise sharply as irrigable land area rises.
Turkey is the sixth largest cotton producer in the world, with output of 837,114 tonnes in 1995/96.
The textile industry, Turkey's top foreign currency earner, exported mainly ready-to-wear items worth about $8 billion in 1995.
